summary.text: Thermodynamics is the branch of physics that deals with heat, work and temperature, and how they relate to energy, entropy and the properties of matter and radiation.
Its behavior is governed by four laws, which describe large-scale measurable quantities and can be explained by the statistics of tiny constituents.
It grew out of efforts to make early steam engines more efficient, and now helps explain engines, chemical reactions, phase transitions and even black holes.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Sparked by the wish to make steam engines more efficient

facts.label: Number of laws
facts.value: Four laws form its axiomatic basis

facts.label: What entropy tells
facts.value: The direction a system can evolve and its state of order

facts.label: Where it applies
facts.value: Engines, phase transitions, chemical reactions and black holes

items.prompt: A cup of hot coffee sits on a desk and slowly cools. Which pair of ideas does thermodynamics use to describe this?

options.label: Heat and temperature, related to energy
Charge and magnetism, related to current
Lenses and mirrors, related to rays
Orbits and gravity, related to curvature

items.explain: Thermodynamics deals with heat, work and temperature, and how these relate to energy and the properties of matter.

items.prompt: Why did early thinkers in this field care about the topic in the first place?

options.label: They wanted to explain why planets follow orbits
They wanted to design better lenses for telescopes
They wanted steam engines to waste less of their fuel
They wanted to map the weather across whole continents

items.explain: Thermodynamics developed from a desire to increase the efficiency of early steam engines, notably through Sadi Carnot's work.

items.prompt: A scientist says the four laws describe measurable big-picture quantities, yet can also be explained by what tiny particles do on average. Which approach does that point to?

options.label: Statistical mechanics, linking microscopic behavior to large-scale results
Geometric optics, treating light as straight-line rays
Electrostatics, studying charges that are held still
Celestial mechanics, tracking the motion of planets

items.explain: The laws use macroscopic quantities but can be explained through microscopic constituents by statistical mechanics, which predicts collective motion from microscopic behavior.

items.prompt: A friend says a messy room is just disorder, nothing a physics law could describe. Which thermodynamic quantity is described as quantifying a system's state of order?

options.label: Internal energy
Temperature
Equation of state
Entropy

items.explain: The second law defines entropy, which describes the direction a system can evolve and quantifies its state of order.

items.prompt: A factory moves energy from burning fuel into moving a machine, with some leaving as heat. Which law's statement fits this?

options.label: Energy can be passed between systems as heat, as work and with matter
Energy can be created from nothing whenever work is done
Heat is a form of matter that cannot become work
Work and heat belong to separate systems that never interact

items.explain: The first law states that energy can be transferred between physical systems as heat, as work, and through the transfer of matter.

items.prompt: A student claims thermodynamics only matters for physicists studying engines. Which reply is best supported?

options.label: It matters only to machines built in the 1800s
It matters in chemistry, cell biology, materials science and more
It matters only to fields that deal with temperature gauges
It matters to physics but not to any practical engineering

items.explain: Its results are essential for other physics fields and for chemistry, engineering, cell biology, biomedical engineering, materials science and economics.
